textes.Bienvenue au Cadran Fêlé, un escape game: Welcome to the Cadran Fêlé, an escape room in Lyon. Rooms, puzzles, game masters, teams, bookings, games and reviews: all its data is here. You help its team: Bérangère, the manager, Jade at the front desk, Malik, who leads the game masters, Théo, the puzzle designer, and Zoé, in charge of reviews and loyalty. Explore the database to solve the missions.

textes.Une ligne par énigme d’une salle : son n: One row per puzzle in a room: its name, its type and its step in the course. A room’s puzzles are solved one after the other, in order.

textes.Une ligne par équipe enregistrée, qu’ell: One row per registered team, whether or not it has played yet: its name, its group type, its city, and the first name, last name and email address of its captain, who books for it.
textes.Une ligne par réservation d’un créneau d: One row per booking of a time slot in a room, for a game planned from January 1 to June 30, 2025: the team, the date and time, the number of players, the price, the channel and the promo code. A team can book several times.
textes.Une ligne par réservation annulée par l’: One row per booking cancelled by the team: the cancellation date, its reason and the amount refunded. A cancelled booking has no game.
textes.Une ligne par partie jouée : le maître d: One row per game played: the game master who ran it, whether the team got out in time, its escape time and the number of hints requested. A game’s room, team and date are those of its booking.
textes.Une ligne par indice donné pendant une p: One row per hint given during a game: the puzzle the team was stuck on and the minute of play at which the game master gave it. A game may have received no hints.
textes.Une ligne par avis laissé par une équipe: One row per review left by a team after its game: its date, its rating from 1 to 5 and, if there is one, its comment. A game has at most one review; some have none.

textes.Le Cadran Fêlé est un escape game de Lyo: The Cadran Fêlé is an escape room in Lyon: a team locks itself in a themed room and has to get out before the time runs out, by solving a series of puzzles. Each room accepts a minimum and a maximum number of players, and its price is per player. One room isn’t open yet: it has no opening date. A family of 6 calls to book. Jade, at the front desk, wants to offer them the open rooms that accept 6 players, from cheapest to most expensive.
